### problem_chain

Root problem, from the persona: put a block of prepaid hours on the account now, priced and credited, the purchase run by the customer himself → `service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price` (computes purchase_amount_usd; tool `purchase_hour_block_a465dc68`, owner user).

Walking the root rule's prerequisite sentence against the world at the opening: "A block of prepaid hours is priced only once the credit ceiling standing on the rate program carries a change dated in the current program year." — program 1730d7a0… carries `last_change_type = primary_site_changed`, `last_change_date = 2025-06-18`, `credit_limit_usd = 75000`, term 2025-12-01 → 2027-11-30: the most recent term change is not a ceiling change and its date precedes the current term → FALSE at the opening. Resolving policy (from the charter alone): the only rule that writes the ceiling, `service_ext_credit_ceiling_review` → `set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3`, which stamps `last_change_type = credit_limit_changed` and `last_change_date = today`. Its own rule carries no prerequisite sentence → leaf.

Derived tree: purchase ← ceiling review (value_input: ceiling_headroom). One prerequisite problem, one value_input edge (floor max(1−1,1) = 1 met), no cycle. Order: ceiling review → purchase.

Load-bearing run: skip the ceiling write (ceiling stays 75,000): headroom 61,000, no excess, no release charge → price 54,030.24 instead of 54,247.92 — bears weight.

No parallel edges. No-wait: the review is a synchronous record write. Tools do not judge prerequisites (`_difficulty.md` §action_binding_and_uuids). Customer's own write: `purchase_hour_block_a465dc68` (owner user), handed over at the agent's direction ("he will take it on when it is handed to him").

Persona raises only the root: he asks for hours priced and credited; he names no ceiling, no review, no other item of work (the queued dispatches are what he wants the hours for, not something he asks the desk to do); "content for the desk to do whatever it has to do on its own side … and says so if he is told there is something to settle first" is conditioned on the agent raising it; he closes on the purchase reference. Charges with a due day in the window: 9,800 (2025-12-31) + 7,200 (2026-03-06) + 6,480 (2026-04-30) + 4,230 (2026-06-10) + 7,200 (2026-06-25) + 5,940 (2026-07-20) + 4,750 (2026-09-06) = 45,600 (INV-40866012 due 2025-10-20 is exactly 10 months back — near-miss excluded). 45,600 > 37,500 and ≤ 75,000 → starting ceiling rounded up to 46,000 (tier 1). Volume: calls dispatched in the window 7 (2025-11-13 at exactly 10 months excluded), emergencies 2 → 7 ≥ 6 → +7,500 (tier 2). Ceiling = 46,000 × (1 + 0.15 + 0.12 − 0.10) + 7,500 = **61,320.00** → `set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3(program_id=1730d7a0…, credit_limit_usd=61320.00)`.

Step 2 — block price (after step 1). Window: rollover tier, 9 < 24 → the 18-month expiry period (tier 1). Blocks within 18 months: 60 (2025-06-15, 15 months — inside) + 60 + 60 = 180 (the 2024-12-10 block at 21 months excluded). Hours drawn within 18 months: 38.0 (2025-04-08, 17 months — inside) + 41.5 + 35.5 + 44.0 + 52.5 + 48.0 + 57.0 + 61.5 + 55.0 + 37.0 = 470.0. ## findings

- **F5 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, charter-global, demonstrated here).** Symptom: three release charges for one purchase. Root cause: the purchase rule subtracts "the open position" from the ceiling without defining it; the compute binds all-time invoiced less all-time paid; the late fee policy defines a twelve-month open position; the program row carries `balance_due`. Evidence: rule sentence "The headroom is the credit ceiling standing on the rate program less the open position"; compute `open_position = invoiced_all - paid_all`; seed `service_programs.1730d7a0….balance_due = 18000` against the ledger's 14,000; `_difficulty.md` §rule_compute_equivalence. Consequence: 54,247.92 / 54,367.92 / 54,030.24. Affected: service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price.rule / compute / compute_basis; scored parameter purchase_amount_usd. Previous revision: none.
- **F6 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, charter-global, demonstrated here).** Symptom: two ceilings. Root cause: payment_record tiers require "no invoice on the program has stood past its due day longer than the tier's suspension period"; the compute tests only the latest-due invoice (12 days) while INV-41041256 (due 2026-07-20, 5,740 unpaid) has stood 60 days and INV-41019983 (due 2026-06-25, 3,510 unpaid) 85 days. Evidence: seed rows for those invoices and their partial payments; compute `days_past_due = DAYS(LATEST(... 'due_date' ...), NOW)`; `_difficulty.md` §rule_compute_equivalence. Consequence: 61,320.00 (compute) vs 54,420.00 (prose), and prices 54,247.92 vs 54,454.92. Affected: service_ext_credit_ceiling_review.rule / compute; scored parameters credit_limit_usd and purchase_amount_usd. Previous revision: none.
- **F4 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, charter-global).** Symptom: `price_basis` has two distinguishable outcomes, not three. Root cause: tier 2 prices "at the rate the block steps to", which for two or three multiples is the block hour rate by the `stepped_block_rate` ladder. Evidence: `_difficulty.md` §factor_ladders. Consequence on this world: none on the scored price (tier 1 taken); the ladder claim fails structurally. Affected: service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price.factors[price_basis] and its rule sentence. Previous revision: none.
- O15 (observation): `balance_due` 18,000 and the ledger's 14,000 disagree; feeds F5.
- O16 (observation): "the current program year" is undefined in the purchase rule; unmet under every reading on this world.
- O17 (observation): `block_hours_remaining = 24.0` agrees with neither base nor extended accounting (both 0).
- O20 / O21 / O22 (observations): the three rationale / contract assertions above that fail recomputation, none of which moves a scored figure.
- Verdicts otherwise: problem tree PASS; derivation equals GT on every item.
